mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret statements that equate two differences as signed equations preserving the order of names on each side; treat each side as a signed difference, allowing negative values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "the number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have" (or similar).
mathgap.example: Treating (A - B) = (C - D) as |A - B| = |C - D|, losing the sign.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and simplify, propagating the information throughout the system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving any equation that yields a concrete value for a variable, immediately replace that variable in all other equations.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known variable unchanged in other equations, causing the system to remain underdetermined.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative and difference statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the text, taking into account any prior transfers or overrides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a statement that compares two persons, use the current values after all earlier statements have been applied.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a comparison that appears after a transfer, ignoring the effect of the transfer.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal subset of equations that involve the queried person directly or indirectly, and solve only that subsystem, ignoring unrelated equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem asks for the count of a specific person, first trace which variables are connected to that person through equations and restrict solving to that subgraph.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire large system of equations even though only a small component is needed, leading to wasted effort.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating similarly spelled names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a new name appears, create a distinct variable unless it is exactly the same string as a previously seen name.
mathgap.example: Confusing "Mackenzie" with "Mackenz" and using a single variable for both.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When a phrase says "the difference between the number of items that A and B have", interpret it as the signed difference A - B, preserving the order of the names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the wording "difference between ... A and B", set up the equation with A first, B second.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "the difference between A and B" as B - A, reversing the intended order.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret "A has K more than B" as A - B = K, and "A has K fewer than B" as A - B = -K, preserving sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative phrase with "more" or "fewer", translate it into a signed equation.
mathgap.example: Swapping the sign for "fewer" and writing A - B = K instead of -K.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N items", set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count statement appears, assign the given number to the person, discarding any earlier inferred value.
mathgap.example: Treating a later "X has N" as an initial count and ignoring the earlier assignment.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer statement in the order given, subtracting the specified amount from the giver and adding it to the receiver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a "X gives K items to Y" statement, update X and Y immediately before handling later statements.
mathgap.example: Applying the second transfer before the first, resulting in incorrect balances.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Evaluation
mathgap.principle: When a statement conditionally transfers items (e.g., "If X has more than Y items, X transfers all items to Z"), first resolve all non-conditional statements to determine X's current count, then evaluate the condition; if true, move X's entire count to Z and set X's count to zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a conditional transfer that depends on a comparison of the giver's count, evaluate the condition after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "If X has more than Y items, X transfers their items to Z" as transferring only the excess over Y, or ignoring the condition entirely.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often interprets "A has K more than B" as B - A = K, reversing the intended direction.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always translate "A has K more than B" to the signed equation A - B = K; similarly, "A has K fewer than B" to A - B = -K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign when converting difference statements, assuming only the magnitude matters.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the sign of each difference; interpret "the difference between A and B" as A - B, not |A - B|.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies all transfers simultaneously or out of order, missing the effect on subsequent statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements sequentially in the order they appear, updating counts after each transfer before handling later statements.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct count statements set the initial value and never get overridden, even if they appear later.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, assign the value at that point, overriding any previous value for that person.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model sometimes reads phrases like "A has twice as many as B" as an addition rather than a multiplication.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize multiplicative language and translate it to a multiplication equation (e.g., A = 2 * B).
